TLDR: I heard a lot of sh!t from others about this game. Then I played it... And it's a good title. Chances are you saw this game, thought to yourself that it was a Left 4 Dead knock off or continuation and you'd be right for both of them. Just get it, the gun play is good, the card system works well when you get used to it and the challenge is much more real than in Left for Dead, there, I said it.

Story: This is my fourth review in an hour so I'm gonna keep it brief. It's Left for Dead but more recent, alright?

Gameplay: Essentially the same as L4D 2 but without the mods. 
The biggest addition to the game is the cards system (instead of a class system); as it allows for buffing certain stats of your character, sometimes at the cost of some other stats. The variety and complexity is rather surprising and has a huge effect and how you can and will approach the game.
The main campaign is up to 4 players coop and there's apparently a PvP mode but if your intention is to buy this game for the PvP you're buying the wrong game here.
Guns have stats, and those stats can be improved by buying parts for it, they are often bought or randomly found throughout the maps. You do NOT get to keep these guns forever so improve it with the one currency you also lose at the end of your levels and get on with your campaign as the real progression is really found in your deck (of cards).
The idea is to build a deck that goes with your gameplay style that will allow you to tackle even more challenging difficulties and earn even more powerful cards to have an even more... You get the idea.
Don't feel too bad on your first runs, the cards really do change everything.

Graphics: Looks good! Nice textures, animations are good, no complaints here.

Audio: From spewing to screaming to shooting, everything is good.

While this game may get a bad rep for its copying of L4D style or the way it advertised itself... Remember, there's people that make money out of being NPCs on tiktok. So it could be a lot worse.

Absolutely not Left 4 Dead 3. Don’t go in expecting similar game play because the two are fundamentally different. While they share a similar theme of surviving against hordes of zombies, this game charts its own path with unique mechanics and pacing. That said, it absolutely stands strong on its own merits. It’s a highly enjoyable experience, especially when played with friends, offering plenty of cathartic fun as you mow down zombies by the dozen. If you’re looking for satisfying, action packed co-op game play, it’s well worth the investment, particularly when you catch it on a discount. Definitely recommended for fans of zombie slaying mayhem!
